crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Judicial Analytics
children.blurb: Judicial analytics applies data analysis to court records, judicial decisions, and litigation events to help lawyers assess likely outcomes, timing, cost, and judge behavior.

children.name: Opposing Counsel and Docket Patterns
children.blurb: This page covers how AI systems read public docket data to profile opposing counsel and identify recurring motion, settlement, and delay patterns.

children.name: Settlement Valuation and Risk
children.blurb: Settlement valuation and risk covers the work of estimating a case's likely settlement range and the probability and severity of adverse outcomes before trial.

children.name: Jury Selection and Public Data
children.blurb: This page covers how public records and data about potential jurors, jury pools, and past verdicts are used to inform jury selection in civil and criminal litigation.

children.name: Live Testimony Cross-Referencing
children.blurb: Live testimony cross-referencing covers the real time comparison of a witness's spoken or written answers against the existing case record, including depositions, prior statements, exhibits, and the testimony of other witnesses.

sections.body: Litigation prediction and judicial analytics uses machine learning to find patterns in court records, rulings, dockets, and public data. In practice, AI now reads past opinions to estimate how a specific judge has ruled on similar motions, flags how often an opposing counsel settles or files extensions, and compares a current case against thousands of past outcomes to suggest a settlement range. It also scans public records and social media for jury pool information and cross-references live testimony against depositions and documents for contradictions. These are assistive tools for lawyers, not oracles.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Judge analytics works reasonably well for high volume courts where a judge has hundreds of published rulings, but it fails for new judges or rare legal questions. Settlement valuation produces ranges with wide error bars because past settlements are often confidential and case facts differ. Jury selection tools can only use public data, so they miss private attitudes and cannot predict how a specific juror will deliberate. Live testimony cross-referencing catches exact wording mismatches but often flags false positives when a witness paraphrases. The site tracks 142 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, which shows that the legal status of these tools is still being fought in court.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader would start with Judicial Analytics to see how a judge has ruled on similar motions and what language they respond to. Opposing Counsel and Docket Patterns then shows how the other side behaves, such as how often they settle, appeal, or ask for delays. Settlement Valuation and Risk turns those patterns into a numeric range and a measure of uncertainty for going to trial. Jury Selection and Public Data covers what can be learned from voter rolls, property records, and public posts before voir dire. Live Testimony Cross-Referencing is for the courtroom itself, where a lawyer can check a witness's words against earlier statements in real time.
